To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prevalence of mental health, substance use, and other behavioral health disorders among primary care patients is substantial and that primary care physicians are not well equipped to manage these disorders.

(1) the prevalence of substance use disorders among adults is high, (2) substance use disorders have serious medical and social consequences, (3) primary care physicians should screen for substance use disorders in adults, (4) screening should be followed by brief intervention or referral to treatment, and (5) primary care physicians need to be aware of and be able to manage withdrawal and overdose.

the American College of Physi-cians recommends that primary care physicians screen for behavioral health conditions, provide brief interventions, and make referrals to behavioral health specialists when necessary; that the primary care physician's role is not to provide all the care needed for behavioral health conditions; and that the integration of behavioral health care into primary care is a work in progress and requires additional research.
